title: Support TLS server name overrides for URL-based admission webhooks
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Support an optional TLS server name override for URL-based admission webhooks, so the hostname used for TLS certificate verification and SNI can be configured independently of the hostname or IP address used to connect.

For example, an optional `tlsServerName` field in `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1` `WebhookClientConfig` could allow:

```yaml
clientConfig:
  url: https://webhook.private.example.net:9443/validate
  tlsServerName: admission.example.com
  caBundle: <PEM-encoded CA bundle>
```

In this example, the API server would connect to `webhook.private.example.net:9443`, send `admission.example.com` as TLS SNI, and verify the server certificate against `admission.example.com` using the configured CA bundle. The HTTP Host header would continue to follow the URL. This field name and placement are illustrative; feedback on the appropriate API/configuration surface would be welcome.

When the override is omitted, existing behavior would be preserved: TLS verification uses the URL hostname. Certificate chain and hostname verification would remain enabled when an override is configured.

### Why is this needed?

A webhook's network connection address and its TLS identity can differ in deployments that use private endpoints, TCP proxies, or environment-specific routing aliases. For example, several clusters may reach the same admission service through different private DNS names, while that service presents a certificate for a stable identity such as `admission.example.com`.

Today, URL-based admission webhooks cannot express that distinction. Operators must arrange for the URL hostname to appear in the certificate's SANs, or arrange DNS/routing so the certificate's hostname reaches the intended endpoint. This couples certificate management to routing names and can require adding environment-specific SANs or coordinating DNS changes whenever a connection endpoint changes.

An explicit TLS server name would allow operators to choose the connection endpoint while continuing to authenticate the intended service identity. Kubernetes already supports this distinction for ordinary kubeconfig clients through `tls-server-name`.

### Current behavior and references

In the upstream source inspected at commit `f0126a827d42264174a7137217b52f622d8e9a98`:

- [`WebhookClientConfig`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f0126a827d42264174a7137217b52f622d8e9a98/staging/src/k8s.io/api/admissionregistration/v1/types.go) exposes `url`, `service`, and `caBundle`, without a TLS server name override.
- The [URL-based webhook client](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f0126a827d42264174a7137217b52f622d8e9a98/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/client.go) copies the resolver's REST configuration and sets the connection host from the URL.
- The [default admission authentication resolver](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f0126a827d42264174a7137217b52f622d8e9a98/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/authentication.go) reads kubeconfig `AuthInfos`; it does not load a cluster's `tls-server-name` setting. Configuring that setting in an admission authentication kubeconfig therefore does not provide this override.

Related historical issue: #52366 concerned setting the service DNS name for service-based admission webhooks. This request concerns an operator-configurable TLS identity for URL-based admission webhooks.

This limitation is blocking us from onboarding a new admission webhook. Our infrastructure supplies a routing hostname for the webhook endpoint, while the serving certificate contains infrastructure-managed service identities. Infrastructure restrictions prevent us from adding custom SANs to that certificate, including the routing hostname. The admission request therefore fails with a certificate hostname mismatch. For example, with hostnames anonymized:

```text
failed to call webhook: Post "https://webhook.private.example.net:9443/mutate-ray-io-v1-rayjob?timeout=10s": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate is valid for admission.example.com, not webhook.private.example.net
```

We need to connect using the supplied routing hostname while verifying the certificate against an existing service identity. URL-based admission webhook configuration currently provides no way to express this. This is a new-webhook onboarding limitation, not a regression. I would appreciate SIG API Machinery feedback on the configuration surface and whether a KEP is appropriate.

/sig api-machinery
/kind feature

title: WAS: exclusive topology placement for PodGroups (one PodGroup per topology domain)
body:
## What would you like to be added?

An exclusive mode for PodGroup topology placement in kube-scheduler: a PodGroup lands in a topology domain (one value of a node label) that no other in-scope PodGroup occupies, and keeps that domain to itself while its pods run there.

JobSet, LeaderWorkerSet (LWS) and DisaggregatedSet each implement this today by injecting pod affinity and anti-affinity. It came up in kubernetes-sigs/lws#1064 (graduating the LWS `exclusive-topology` annotation to a spec field), where the suggestion was to raise it here instead of implementing it in each controller. This issue asks a question; it does not propose an API.

### What KEP-5732 covers

`TopologyConstraint{Key}` puts all pods of one PodGroup in one domain. Its doc comment says "Different PodGroups can land on different domain instances" ([KEP-5732](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/e3340bf8f7eaa2566ff962fa425ec35d42a6d793/keps/sig-scheduling/5732-topology-aware-workload-scheduling/README.md#L252-L258), [v1beta1 types.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7708623c1a6c115ef1fd4f5f90b98cb7c49d337e/staging/src/k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1beta1/types.go#L858-L868)). Nothing keeps another PodGroup out of that domain, and in the KEP review a reviewer noted that PodGroup replicas may land in different domains "but they can also share them" ([comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5733#discussion_r2610398971), [reply](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5733#discussion_r2623294009)). Exclusivity is not among the KEP's [Goals](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/e3340bf8f7eaa2566ff962fa425ec35d42a6d793/keps/sig-scheduling/5732-topology-aware-workload-scheduling/README.md#L137-L151) or [Future Extensions](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/e3340bf8f7eaa2566ff962fa425ec35d42a6d793/keps/sig-scheduling/5732-topology-aware-workload-scheduling/README.md#L474-L508). I did not find an existing issue asking for it.

### Requested semantics

For a PodGroup G with exclusive placement on node label key K:

1. All scheduled pods of G are on nodes with the same value d of K. This is what `TopologyConstraint` does today.
2. G is placed only in a domain that holds no pods of another in-scope PodGroup, and while G has pods in d, no other in-scope PodGroup is placed in d.
3. d is chosen for the whole group: at least `minCount` pods must fit, as KEP-5732 Phase 2 already checks for each Placement under the Gang policy ([README.md:377-386](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/e3340bf8f7eaa2566ff962fa425ec35d42a6d793/keps/sig-scheduling/5732-topology-aware-workload-scheduling/README.md#L377-L386)).
4. It is a hard constraint checked at scheduling time only, like `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution`.

"In-scope" is the open part, and the three controllers define it differently:

| Controller | Unit | Kept out of the domain | How |
|---|---|---|---|
| JobSet, [`alpha.jobset.sigs.k8s.io/exclusive-topology`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/jobset/blob/a4fae2847493efda10cc427a572a778bf2f1fe1a/api/jobset/v1alpha2/jobset_types.go#L42-L48) | child Job | pods of any other JobSet Job at the same priority, all namespaces | required affinity and anti-affinity on the leader pod ([pod_webhook.go:117-162](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/jobset/blob/a4fae2847493efda10cc427a572a778bf2f1fe1a/pkg/webhooks/pod_webhook.go#L117-L162)); followers get the leader's domain as a nodeSelector ([:164-198](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/jobset/blob/a4fae2847493efda10cc427a572a778bf2f1fe1a/pkg/webhooks/pod_webhook.go#L164-L198)) |
| LWS, [`exclusive-topology` and `subgroup-exclusive-topology`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/api/leaderworkerset/v1/leaderworkerset_types.go#L28-L34) | replica, or subgroup | pods of any other LWS replica (or subgroup) in the same namespace | required affinity and anti-affinity ([pod_webhook.go:255-297](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/pkg/webhooks/pod_webhook.go#L255-L297)); at replica level only the leader carries them and workers get the leader's domain as a nodeSelector ([pod_controller.go:298-309](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/pkg/controllers/pod_controller.go#L298-L309)) |
| DisaggregatedSet, [`placementPolicy.type: ExclusiveTopology`](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/api/disaggregatedset/v1/disaggregatedset_types.go#L147-L183) | slice (one copy of every role, across several LWS) | pods of any other DisaggregatedSet slice in the same namespace | required affinity and anti-affinity on every pod ([affinity.go](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/pkg/utils/disaggregatedset/affinity.go#L37-L103)) |

In all three, pods without the controller's labels (for example a plain Deployment) can still share the domain unless taints are used ([DisaggregatedSet docs](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/site/content/en/docs/concepts/disaggregatedset/placement-policy/_index.md#L43-L45)).

## Why is this needed?

Emulating exclusivity with pod affinity in each controller has known problems:

1. **No look-ahead.** The leader (JobSet, LWS) or the first pod (DisaggregatedSet) commits the domain, and the rest of the group stays Pending if it does not fit. KEP-5732 rejects pod inter-affinity for this reason ([Alternatives](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/e3340bf8f7eaa2566ff962fa425ec35d42a6d793/keps/sig-scheduling/5732-topology-aware-workload-scheduling/README.md#L935-L946)), and the DisaggregatedSet KEP documents the same risk and defers to gang scheduling ([KEP-848](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/keps/848-disaggregatedset-placement-policy/README.md#L194-L201)).
2. **No gang scheduling together with exclusivity.** LWS alpha rejects gang or WAS topology constraints combined with `exclusive-topology` ([KEP-666 rule 10](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/keps/666-gang-scheduling-in-lws/README.md#L544-L546), [phase_one.go](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/pkg/schedulerprovider/phase_one.go#L451-L453)). JobSet's docs say native gang scheduling will enable more robust topology-aware scheduling, which they call the core objective of the exclusive topology feature ([tpu_multislice.md](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/jobset/blob/a4fae2847493efda10cc427a572a778bf2f1fe1a/site/content/en/docs/tasks/tpu_multislice.md#L35)). The LWS docs ask users to pick either native exclusive placement or Kueue TAS bin-packing ([LWS docs](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/lws/blob/8dd3fd54dd4f286bf115d9214372970633dcaae8/site/content/en/docs/examples/leaderworkerset/topology-aware-scheduling/_index.md#L19-L29)).
3. **Cost.** The Kubernetes docs advise against inter-pod affinity in clusters larger than several hundred nodes ([assign-pod-node.md](https://github.com/kubernetes/website/blob/1c7aa9955e884879397ed15de88605f05eb61d1f/content/en/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node.md#L261-L263)). JobSet measured 58 vs 266 pods/s at 5,000 nodes with its exclusive-placement affinities (kubernetes-sigs/jobset#174), then moved to leader-only terms (kubernetes-sigs/jobset#310) and added a manual node-label and taint mode (kubernetes-sigs/jobset#312). DisaggregatedSet still puts the terms on every pod.
4. **Controller machinery.** JobSet rejects follower pod creation until the leader is scheduled, which loads the API server (kubernetes-sigs/jobset#482). It also needed race handling (kubernetes-sigs/jobset#341) and limited exclusivity to the same priority level as part of supporting preemption (kubernetes-sigs/jobset#682, kubernetes-sigs/jobset#687).
5. **Other placers cannot see it.** Kueue TAS picks nodes without seeing the injected anti-affinity, so it can assign exclusive LWS pods a domain their anti-affinity forbids (kubernetes-sigs/kueue#15057). The direction suggested there is the WAS integration (kubernetes-sigs/kueue#13149). Kueue TAS Topology Spreading caps a domain's share within one spreading group to a value in (0, 1), so it does not exclude other workloads ([KEP-13746](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/blob/df693920cb4be96ed909ab2292966a1c7635800e/keps/13746-tas-topology-spreading/README.md#L460-L463)).
6. **Diverging definitions.** Scope has been argued separately in each project (kubernetes-sigs/lws#539, kubernetes-sigs/jobset#1057). Graduating each controller's version on its own (kubernetes-sigs/lws#1064) would fix three different scopes into three APIs.

## Question for the WG

Should WAS support exclusive topology placement for PodGroups in kube-scheduler, so controllers can express it through their PodGroup topology constraints instead of injecting pod affinity?

If yes, scope needs a single answer: same namespace or cluster-wide, PodGroups only or all pods, whether priority matters, and whether it applies to CompositePodGroups (a DisaggregatedSet slice spans several LWS).

The answer will inform whether LWS graduates its annotation to its own spec field or maps it onto WAS (kubernetes-sigs/lws#1064). I will add this to the WG meeting agenda.

KEP: kubernetes/enhancements#5732
Related: kubernetes-sigs/lws#1064, kubernetes-sigs/kueue#15057, #136207

/sig scheduling
/sig apps
/wg workload-aware-scheduling
/kind feature

title: Tracking: investigate and document deprecated label usage related to KEP-837
body:
[KEP-837](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/837) defines the promotion of topology related labels and a subsequent deprecation. As defined by the KEP:

The 3 deprecated labels are:
beta.kubernetes.io/instance-type
failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone
failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region

They should be renamed to:
node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
topology.kubernetes.io/zone
topology.kubernetes.io/region

Given the length of time that these labels have been deprecated, but not removed, SIG Cloud Provider is restarting the deprecation cycle on these labels. To start the process we will identify the current of uses of the deprecated labels in the kubernetes code and the kubernetes website. Identifying current uses is the first step in a plan to warn users about the deprecation, provide advice about how to monitor usage in clusters, and a method to ratchet the removal.

This issue is purely to track the progress of identifying places where the deprecated labels are still being used.

title: Burndown: Quantity int64 overflow and checked accessors
body:
This tracks ongoing and planned work to fix `resource.Quantity`'s int64 accessor overflow behavior.

## Goal

Make `resource.Quantity` a value type that is safe to share between goroutines and correct for every input it accepts.

- Value type semantics. Changing a Quantity never changes another copy of it.
- Read-only methods never modify the Quantity, so concurrent reads are safe.
- Every method returns the same result whether the value is stored as int64 or `inf.Dec`.
- Arithmetic never wraps, and accessors report overflow or saturate.
- No input can make an operation use excessive CPU or take a long time to complete.
- Serialized output always reflects the current value and format.
- Data written by earlier releases still decodes, and every tightened check reuses one ratchet so existing objects stay updatable.
- Every fixed behavior and every open gap is pinned by a test on both backends.

## Known Gaps

| Expression | Returns | Gap |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NewScaledQuantity(MaxInt64, 1).Value()` | `-10` | multiply wraps around 64 bits |
| `MustParse("100E").Value()` | `0` | conversion fails internally and falls back to zero |
| `MustParse("9223372036854775808").Value()`| `MinInt64` | barely-too-large value becomes negative |
| `MustParse("-9.5Gi").Value()` | `8246196746` | bug in unsigned math flips the sign (#138510) |
| `NewQuantity(MinInt64).Neg()` | `MinInt64` | −MinInt64 doesn't fit in int64, so negation silently does nothing |
| `zero.Sub(MinInt64 quantity)` | `MinInt64` | similar to above, but using `.Sub()` instead of `.Neg()` |
| `MustParse("1000E").String()` | `"1"` | serialization drops the suffix for decimal values above 10^18 (#140459) |
| `ParseQuantity("1e4294967297")` | `10`, no error | exponent is truncated to 32 bits (2³²+1 → 1), should be parse error; #141203 rejected it, which created the decode row below; #142395 restores the 1.37 truncation for compatibility (09-24 decision); rejecting it is left to the 1.39 create-time bound |
| `NewQuantity(MinInt64).Neg(); q.AsInt64()` | `(MinInt64, true)` | `AsInt64` reports ok=true for a value that isn't the true result of the operation; same after `zero.Sub(MinInt64 quantity)` |
| `MustParse("1e100").Value()` vs `MustParse("1e100").ToDec().Value()` | `0` vs `MinInt64` | same input, different wrong values on the int64 vs Dec backends; fixes must land on both paths |
| decode of `"1e4294967296"` written by a <=1.37 apiserver | error, object undecodable | 1.37 truncated the exponent, kept value 1 and stored the spelling verbatim in JSON and proto; master rejects it in ParseQuantity (#141203); the etcd3 store fails the whole LIST on the first undecodable object. #142395 (approved 09-24) narrows the exponent the way 1.37 did, so these decode to the 1.37 value and keep their stored spelling; an exponent that narrows to MinInt32 still errors |
| `MustParse("1e2147483647").Add(MustParse("1"))` | hangs | the inf.Dec fallback aligns scales by writing 10^delta digits; same at Sub, AsScale/RoundUp, BinarySI String, AsFloat64Slow and DRA `quantityKeyAsDec`; reachable through pod-level resources validation and ResourceQuota admission; present in v1.37 and earlier |
| `MustParse("1e2147483647").Add(MustParse("1n"))` | `2e-9` | `int64Amount.Add/Sub` compute the scale delta in int32 and wrap instead of falling back; Cmp got this fix in #142013, Add/Sub did not |

## Task List

  - [x] #138309: parse boundary tests (18/19/20 digits, MinInt64/MaxInt64 +/- 1)
  - [x] #140556, #140518, #140702: shared inf.Dec state (aliasing) fixes for #140744
  - [x] #141170: baseline test matrix; each wrong-today field carries a TODO for its fixed value; suite green on master so it doubles as the burndown tracker
  - [x] #138510: scaledValue negative rounding + tests
  - [x] #140459: String() suffix drop for DecimalSI > 10^18
      - [x] #141817: regression from #140459. BinarySI values >= 1024 that are not a multiple of 1024 serialize in e notation when divisible by 10
  - [x] #140674: MaxMilliQuantity + overflow docs
  - [x] #138507: EBNF grammar fix for integer exponents
  - [x] #141264: fix MinInt64 Neg/Sub via decimal fallback; extreme source scales tracked separately
  - [x] #141169: switch validateBasicResource to Sign() < 0
  - [x] #141181: stop using Value() overflow to detect sign or unset limits in csi_client.go and eviction
  - [x] Checked-accessor contract settled: (int64, ok bool), saturate at the sign-correct rail, round away from zero
  - [x] #141305: add AsScaledInt64/AsMilliInt64, switch Value/MilliValue/ScaledValue to saturating wrappers, bound int64MultiplyScale*/scaledValue
  - [x] #141937: AsApproximateFloat64 NaN for zero at large scale
  - [x] #141938: MustParse near MaxInt64. Skew note: CEL isInteger()/asInteger() start returning true/values for 19-digit quantities.
  - [x] #141203: reject exponents that don't fit in int32 (1e4294967297)
  - [x] #142013: Cmp bounding
  - [x] #141201: regression test for Scale(MinInt32).infScale() sign edge case
  - [x] #141980: clear cached serialization when JSON/CBOR null resets a Quantity
  - [x] #142395: objects written by a <=1.37 apiserver with an out-of-int32 exponent (e.g. `cpu: 1e4294967296`) fail to decode on master since #141203
  - [ ] #142104: AsInt64 behavior should be the same on both backends (on hold until the work below lands; see #142576)
      - [x] #142576: AsInt64 tests from #142104, merged first as guard rails (merged 09-30)
      - [x] #142581: Cmp, AsDec and AsFloat64Slow no longer modify the Quantity, so all read methods are safe to call concurrently; follow-up to #142277 (merged 10-01)
      - [x] #142594: an inf.Dec Quantity behaves as a value type, like the int64 form; `b := a; a.Add(x)` no longer changes `b` (merged 10-02)
      - [x] #142603: NewDecimalQuantity copies the caller's inf.Dec instead of sharing it (merged 10-02)
      - [x] #142624: AsInt64 test coverage on both backends (merged 10-02)
      - [x] #142635: RoundUp test coverage on both backends (merged 10-06)
      - [x] #142744: widenedScale type to make the int64 and inf.Dec scale arithmetic explicit; refactor only (merged 10-07)
      - [x] #142764: the cached string records the Format it was written for, and reads ignore it after Format changes (merged 10-07)
  - [ ] #141306: bound work when parsing sub-nano quantities. Also fixes int32 scale wrap on the fast path and the unbounded nano padding for long mantissas at large positive exponents
  - [ ] #142156: fix canonical exponent overflow (q := MustParse("1000e2147483647"); q.String() returns "1e-2147483646")

  - [ ] TODO: bound all scale-alignment call sites

      - [ ] TODO: kubelet emptyDir desired size limit: an ephemeral-storage limit past int64 must mean no limit, not MaxInt64
      - [ ] #142369 (@AryanKansagara, needs ok-to-test): csi_client NodeExpandVolume must reject a size past int64 before the CSI call
      - [ ] #142334: CalculateTimeoutForVolume capped at MaxInt32

      - [x] #142171 (@semx, rebased onto master 09-18 after #142170 merged): LimitRanger skips min/max/ratio for container and pod-level resources a resize leaves unchanged
      - [x] #142190 (@thc1006): ResourceQuota update skips the #141349 integer check for spec.hard, status.hard and status.used values the object already stores
      - [x] #142193 (@thc1006): tests for the #142190 status.hard fallback to the stored spec.hard (stale stored status; a new spec.hard in the same request must not match)
  - [x] #140135: OpenAPI description CommonMark formatting
  - [x] #142052 (@krishhna24): golden String/JSON/CBOR/proto tests; lifts the hold on #138166
  - [ ] TODO: CEL isInteger()/asInteger() coverage for 19-digit quantities (#141938)
  - [ ] #138166 (@tgao26, fixes #138165): canonicalization of fractional decimal inputs; hold lifted when #142052 merged 09-16; needs rebase, no push since 04-02 and no reply to the 09-17 rebase request; takeover candidate; must stay backward compatible; 1.39 with the spelling decision
  - [ ] TODO: tests that would have caught the regressions above before merge (test-only PRs; need owners):
      - [ ] exact-oracle law test against math/big.Rat plus a boundary grid (digit counts, int64 rails, exponents at the int32 edges, all suffixes, both backends) in the resource package, with per-case timeouts so a hang is a red test; merge gate for further library changes
      - [ ] accept/reject golden generated once from v1.37.0 for every Quantity check (integer, hugepages, Sign, LimitRange ratio, LimitRanger, DRA), so a PR that flips a cell owes a ratchet or a deferral
      - [ ] stored-data test: write 1.37-storable extreme bodies straight to etcd and assert GET, LIST, WATCH, unchanged PUT and status PUT succeed for every Quantity-bearing kind (the existing apidefinitions unconditional-update test uses "1M"-class values and no status subresources)
      - [ ] forbidigo rule for Value/MilliValue/ScaledValue in pkg/apis/*/validation, plugin/pkg/admission, pkg/registry and quota

## Exit criteria

An item is done when it has a merged fix with regression coverage, or an explicit deferral to a linked follow-up issue with an owner. The tracker closes when every task-list line is one of those two. 1.38 code freeze is Nov 16; anything without lgtm and an approver by Nov 2 is deferred to a linked 1.39 follow-up rather than held open.

Out of scope: #140744 and #141404 (shallow-copy detection and the read-mutation data race, separate effort; #142277 (@pohly) is the fix for #141404 and changes when ParseQuantity caches a string, which bears on the String() fast-path TODO above), #137590 (parse-format widening), #131972 (CRD formats), #142364 (gopkg.in/inf.v0 is unmaintained; relevant to any representation change, not to this list), a create-time bound on Quantity magnitude and precision (1.39 KEP, warn first).

title: Ensure Credential Pulled Images tests still flaking with "pulled record ... never appeared" after #138527/#138642 (kubelet-gce-e2e-swap-ubuntu-serial)
body:
Title
Ensure Credential Pulled Images tests still flaking with "pulled record ... never appeared" after 
#138527/
#138642

Body

Hitting this on kubelet-gce-e2e-swap-ubuntu-serial - pretty sure this is the same flake as 
#136546/
#138527, just came back.

Testgrid: https://testgrid.k8s.io/sig-node-kubelet#kubelet-gce-e2e-swap-ubuntu-serial

A few sub-tests under Ensure Credential Pulled Images ... [FeatureGate:KubeletEnsureSecretPulledImages] are failing, all through the same shared BeforeEach helper (tempRemoveImagePulledRecord in test/e2e_node/util_kubeletconfig.go):

util_kubeletconfig.go:133] Unexpected error: the file with the pulled record for the image ID never appeared:
<context.deadlineExceededError>: context deadline exceeded
Quick rundown of what that helper does: it polls every 1s for up to 5s waiting for kubelet to write an ImagePulledRecord at /var/lib/kubelet/image_manager/pulled/sha256-<hash>, then moves it aside so a later step can check kubelet's behavior when the record's missing. If nothing shows up in 5s, it just fails.

#138527 got closed by 
#138642, but looking at that PR, it only added debug logging to this wait loop - didn't touch the 5s timeout or actually figure out why the record's sometimes missing. So this was never really fixed, just made easier to see happening.

And that's actually how I found something new - the extra logging from 
#138642 caught this in a recent run (2026-07-25, ~12:40 UTC) that wasn't visible back when 
#138527 was filed:

util_kubeletconfig.go:116] failed to stat file ".../pulled/sha256-c0a25c4ccec43320c35febdf68a46e03b3f9323eada881535d78d91aa9962741": ... no such file or directory
util_kubeletconfig.go:128] contents of "/var/lib/kubelet/image_manager/pulled": map[
  .../pulled/sha256-fbeb66043fabeed6f125049e44aef32e0b8f9e657a240b5a2091b292bab530f2:
    {"kind":"ImagePulledRecord", ..., "lastUpdatedTime":"2026-07-25T14:26:20Z", ...}
]
So at the moment it fails, the pulled/ directory isn't actually empty - there's a record in there, just for a different image, written ~23 minutes earlier by (presumably) an earlier sub-test in the same run. The record this specific check is waiting for just never shows up in the 5s window.

That makes me think this isn't pure slowness - more likely kubelet just doesn't write a new ImagePulledRecord at all when the image's already cached from an earlier sub-test in the same run, and the poll is timing out waiting for something that was never coming. Would be good to get sig-node's take on whether that's expected - if so, the fix is probably on the test's assumptions, not the timeout.

Checked the last 10 Testgrid columns for this job (~07-24 to 07-26) - failed 3/10 times, 6/20 over a longer window, so it's a real recurring thing, not a one-off. One specific run if useful: prow job 2080994746846679040 (2026-07-25, ~12:40-14:49 UTC), 2 sub-tests failed with this exact error.

/sig node
/kind flake

Related: 
#136546, 
#138527, 
#138642

title: kubectl get: PrintObj errors are silently discarded in human-readable output loop
body:
### What happened?

When running kubectl get pods -o yaml (or any human-readable/structured output that goes through the per-object printer loop), errors returned by printer.PrintObj are silently discarded. The loop in Run() that iterates over fetched objects calls printer.PrintObj(info.Object, w) without checking the error return value, so a broken pipe, a closed writer, or any other IO failure during output is invisible to the caller. the command exits 0 regardless.

Relevant code:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/main/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/get/get.go#L569

```go
for _, info := range infos {
    ...
    printer.PrintObj(info.Object, w) // error return ignored
}
```


This is notable because the surrounding function already has an error-aggregation mechanism in place for this exact purpose. ToPrinter errors a few lines earlier are collected into an allErrs[] error slice and returned via utilerrors.NewAggregate(allErrs) at the end of Run(). The plumbing exists; PrintObj's return value just isn't fed into it.

A second occurrence of the identical pattern exists at staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/apply/prune.go#L137 printer.PrintObj(obj, p.out) inside a loop, in a function that returns error, with the result likewise ignored.



### What did you expect to happen?

Any error from printer.PrintObj in the loop should be captured, added to allErrs, and ultimately returned via the existing utilerrors.NewAggregate(allErrs) call, causing the command to exit non-zero consistent with how the ToPrinter error path in the same function already behaves:


```go
if err := printer.PrintObj(info.Object, w); err != nil {
    if !errs.Has(err.Error()) {
        errs.Insert(err.Error())
        allErrs = append(allErrs, err)
    }
}
```


### How can we reproduce it?

The easiest way to trigger this in a real cluster is to pipe the output to a program that exits early (causing a broken pipe):

```console
$ kubectl get pods -A | head -1
```


On Linux this triggers a broken-pipe write error at the OS level, but kubectl will still exit 0 because the error from PrintObj is swallowed.

A unit test can inject a writer that returns an error to confirm the bug programmatically.

### Anything else we need to know?

The fix is small: wrap the PrintObj call in the loop with the same error-collection pattern already used for ToPrinter errors a few lines above it in the same function. The same bug class exists in apply/prune.go:137 and should ideally be fixed alongside this, or filed as a linked follow-up.
Existing tests for get.go's output path cover the happy path only; none inject a failing writer, so this isn't caught by the current suite. A test covering printer-error propagation should be added with the fix.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.35.7
Kustomize Version: v5.7.1
```

</details>

title: Improve init container startup status visibility ( like pulling big image)
body:
### What would you like to be added?


Improve startup status visibility for init containers.

Today, `kubectl get pod` shows the same status for different stages:

```text
Init:0/1
```

For example:

- pulling the init container image
- creating the init container
- running the init container

Also, `initContainerStatuses` may only show:

```yaml
state:
  waiting:
    reason: PodInitializing
```

while the image is still being pulled.

It would be useful to distinguish these stages, similar to `ContainerCreating` for main containers.

For example:

```text
Init:Pulling
Init:ContainerCreating
Init:0/1
```

The exact status names are open for discussion.

Related:
- kubernetes/enhancements#5334 (KEP-5334: Image Pull Progress)
- kubernetes/enhancements#3542 (earlier image pull progress proposal)


### Why is this needed?


When an init container takes a long time to start or run, users cannot tell whether it is pulling the image, creating the container, or already running.

We had an init container image pull that took more than 50 minutes. `kubectl get pod` showed `Init:0/1`, and `initContainerStatuses` only showed `PodInitializing`.

The actual image pulling state was only visible from Pod Events.

This makes troubleshooting init containers harder than main containers.

/sig node
/sig cli

title: kubectl describe pod does not show env vars sourced from valueFrom.fileKeyRef
body:
### What happened?

`kubectl describe pod` prints nothing for a container env var whose source is `valueFrom.fileKeyRef` (KEP-3721 / `EnvFiles`, beta and on by default since v1.35, GA on master). The variable does not appear under `Environment:` at all, not even its name. Env vars with a plain `value`, or with `configMapKeyRef`, `secretKeyRef`, `fieldRef` and `resourceFieldRef`, are printed as usual.

Cause: `describeContainerEnvVars` switches over the `EnvVarSource` kinds it knows about and has no case for `FileKeyRef` (and no `default`), so the entry is silently skipped:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L1990-L2013

### What did you expect to happen?

The variable to be listed in the same style as the other key references, for example:

```
    Environment:
      PLAIN:  1
      TOKEN:  <set to the key 'TOKEN' of file 'app.env' in volume 'config'>  Optional: false
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: envfile
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  initContainers:
  - name: writer
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo TOKEN=abc > /data/app.env"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /data
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "env; sleep 3600"]
    env:
    - name: PLAIN
      value: "1"
    - name: TOKEN
      valueFrom:
        fileKeyRef:
          volumeName: config
          path: app.env
          key: TOKEN
    volumeMounts:
    - name: config
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: config
    emptyDir: {}
```

```console
$ kubectl apply -f pod.yaml
$ kubectl describe pod envfile | grep -A2 'Environment:'
    Environment:
      PLAIN:  1
    Mounts:
```

`TOKEN` is missing, although `kubectl exec envfile -- env` shows `TOKEN=abc`.

At the unit level, calling `describeContainerEnvVars` with a container whose only env var has `ValueFrom.FileKeyRef` set produces just the `Environment:` header. A regression test that fails against the `v1.37.0` tag is in the linked PR.

### Anything else we need to know?

Someone debugging an env-file-backed pod can easily conclude from `describe` that the variable is not set. The fix is a one-case addition to the switch; PR to follow.

title: kubectl explain: add an -o skeleton output format for a copy-pasteable YAML starting point
body:
cc @kubernetes/sig-cli-feature-requests

## What would you like to be added?

A new `kubectl explain <type> -o skeleton` output format that renders a
resource's schema as a concise, editable YAML skeleton (field names with
placeholder values) instead of the verbose field-by-field prose that
`plaintext`/`plaintext-openapiv2` produce.

A companion `-o skeleton-comments` renders the same skeleton with short
inline `# ...` comments for fields that need explaining: `# required`,
`# enum: A|B|C`, `# map[string]string`, and a drill-down hint for fields
collapsed for depth (see below).

Example, `kubectl explain deployments.spec.template.spec.containers -o skeleton`:

```yaml
containers:
- name: "<required>"
  args:
  - ""
  command:
  - ""
  env: []
  envFrom: []
  image: ""
  imagePullPolicy: ""
  lifecycle: {}
  livenessProbe: {}
  ports: []
  readinessProbe: {}
  resources: {}
  securityContext: {}
  startupProbe: {}
  stdin: false
  stdinOnce: false
  terminationMessagePath: ""
  terminationMessagePolicy: ""
  tty: false
  volumeDevices: []
  volumeMounts: []
  workingDir: ""
```

Design notes:
- Placeholder values come from the schema's own `default`, else the first
  `enum` value, else `example`, else a type-appropriate zero value. A
  required field with none of those (typically a bare string) gets the
  literal `"<required>"` sentinel so it isn't mistaken for an intentionally
  empty optional field.
- The `status` subresource and server-managed `metadata` fields
  (`resourceVersion`, `uid`, `managedFields`, etc.) are omitted, since nobody
  hand-authors those.
- To keep output readable on resources with deep optional structure (Pod's
  `affinity`/`tolerations`/`securityContext`, CRD validation schemas), each
  optional field spends against a small budget before its own optional
  children collapse to a placeholder with a drill-down hint (e.g.
  `# optional, nested further -- see: kubectl explain pods.spec.affinity -o skeleton`).
  Required fields are free, so a load-bearing chain like
  `containers[].image` always expands regardless of depth.
- Implemented as one more template in the existing `pkg/explain/v2`
  template-based generator (same mechanism as `plaintext-openapiv2`), so it
  only touches the openapiv3 explain path.

## Why is this needed?

`kubectl explain` today is documentation-first: it's great for looking up
what a field means, but not for the common case of "I want to write a
Deployment/CRD manifest and need a skeleton to fill in." Today's next-best
alternatives (`kubectl create deployment ... --dry-run=client -o yaml`,
hand-copying from docs, or `explain --recursive`) either only cover a
handful of built-in kinds, produce output flooded with every field
regardless of relevance, or don't work at all for CRDs.

`-o skeleton` gives a fast, copy-pasteable starting point for any resource
the cluster serves an OpenAPI v3 schema for, including CRDs, while staying
short enough to read. The optional-depth budget means you see the fields
that actually need decisions (`containers[].image`) without also seeing
every leaf of `affinity`/`tolerations` you probably don't need today, and
you can always drill into a collapsed field with a normal
`explain <type>.<field> -o skeleton` call.

This is proposed as a proof of concept with a working implementation and
test suite already in hand (unit tests covering required/optional
ordering, enums, maps, `$ref` cycles, field-path drill-down, and the
depth-budget behavior). Happy to open the PR once there's SIG CLI agreement
on the approach/flag naming.

title: ParseToLabelSelector rejects "!=", so kubectl create pdb and kubectl set selector fail on selectors that work with kubectl get -l
body:
### What happened?

`metav1.ParseToLabelSelector` rejects the `!=` operator, so the kubectl commands that build a `LabelSelector` from a user-supplied selector string fail on a selector that works everywhere else:

```console
$ kubectl create pdb web-pdb --selector='app!=web' --min-available=1
error: "!=" is not a valid label selector operator

$ kubectl set selector service web 'app!=web'
error: "!=" is not a valid label selector operator

$ kubectl get pods -l 'app!=web'     # works
```

`labels.Parse` accepts `key!=value`, but `ParseToLabelSelector`, whose comment says it "should be kept in sync with the parser in pkg/labels/selector.go", has no case for `selection.NotEquals` and falls through to the default error (only `>` / `<` are rejected deliberately):
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.37.0/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/helpers.go#L117-L144

`key!=value` selects exactly the objects that `key notin (value)` selects (`labels.Requirement.Matches` treats both as "key absent, or value not in the set"), so it can be represented losslessly as `LabelSelectorOpNotIn` with a single value. The reverse direction, `LabelSelectorAsSelector`, already turns `NotIn` back into a selector with the same semantics.

Callers in kubectl: `kubectl create pdb` (`create_pdb.go`) and `kubectl set selector` (`set_selector.go`).

### What did you expect to happen?

The selector is accepted and produces:

```yaml
selector:
  matchExpressions:
  - key: app
    operator: NotIn
    values: ["web"]
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run either command above against any cluster, or call `metav1.ParseToLabelSelector("foo!=bar")`. A regression test that fails against the `v1.37.0` tag is in the linked PR; it also checks that every parsed `LabelSelector` selects the same label sets as the original selector string.

### Anything else we need to know?

Long-standing; the function has never handled `NotEquals`. PR to follow (one `case` in the switch plus tests).

body:
### What happened?

`kubectl describe pod` prints nothing for a projected volume source of type `clusterTrustBundle` or `podCertificate`. The volume is listed, but the block ends after the `Type:` line, so there is no indication of what is actually projected into the pod:

```
Volumes:
  creds:
    Type:  Projected (a volume that contains injected data from multiple sources)
```

Projected sources of type `secret`, `configMap`, `downwardAPI` and `serviceAccountToken` are printed as usual.

Both of the affected sources are GA and on by default since v1.37 (`ClusterTrustBundleProjection` and `PodCertificateRequest` in `pkg/features/kube_features.go`, both marked `LockToDefault in 1.38`), so this is not gated-off output.

Cause: `printProjectedVolumeSource` is an `if / else if` chain over the four source kinds it knows about, with no branch for `ClusterTrustBundle` or `PodCertificate` and no fallback, so those entries are silently skipped:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/58cd835870c09a025a9ee4974ec5d8e9e2415e25/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go#L1076-L1097

`describeVolumes` itself already handles every `VolumeSource` kind and has a `default: <unknown>` arm; only the per-projection switch is incomplete.

### What did you expect to happen?

The projected sources to be listed in the same style as the other kinds, for example:

```
Volumes:
  creds:
    Type:                          Projected (a volume that contains injected data from multiple sources)
    ClusterTrustBundleName:        my-bundle
    Path:                          trust-bundle.pem
    Optional:                      false
    PodCertificateSignerName:      example.com/signer
    KeyType:                       ED25519
    CredentialBundlePath:          credentials.pem
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

No cluster feature configuration is needed on v1.37+. Create a pod with a projected volume:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: projected-creds
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: creds
      mountPath: /var/run/creds
  volumes:
  - name: creds
    projected:
      sources:
      - clusterTrustBundle:
          name: my-bundle
          path: trust-bundle.pem
      - podCertificate:
          signerName: example.com/signer
          keyType: ED25519
          credentialBundlePath: credentials.pem
```

```console
$ kubectl describe pod projected-creds | grep -A5 Volumes:
```

The `creds:` block stops after the `Type:` line.

At the unit level, describing a pod whose only volume is a projected volume with a `clusterTrustBundle` source produces output containing neither the bundle name nor the path.

### Anything else we need to know?

This is the same class of gap as #142208 (`fileKeyRef` missing from the container env output): a source kind added to the API without a matching arm in the describer.

`podCertificate` is the more user-visible of the two, since a pod does not start until certificates have been issued for every `podCertificate` source in its spec, and `kubectl describe pod` is the first place an operator looks when a pod is stuck.

I have a fix with unit tests and will open a PR shortly.

/kind bug
/sig cli
/area kubectl

```console
Reproduced against master at 58cd835870c09a025a9ee4974ec5d8e9e2415e25.
```

title: kubectl cp --retries does not resume when the exec returns an error
body:
#### What happened?

`kubectl cp --retries=N` resumes a copy only when the exec that runs `tar` ends with a nil error. `TarPipe.initReadFrom` runs the exec in a goroutine with `cmdutil.CheckErr(t.o.execute(options))`, so any error from the session exits kubectl before `TarPipe.Read` gets to retry; the resume only happens after the pipe was closed without an error.

Over WebSocket (the default since 1.30) a cut connection ends the exec with `error reading from error stream: ... close 1006`, so `--retries` has not resumed after a cut there. Over SPDY a cut ended the exec with nil, which is the client-go half of #142376 and the only reason `--retries` resumed. With the client-go change from that issue (part 1 of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/142376#issuecomment-6003529603) a cut over SPDY is an error too, and `--retries` stops resuming there as well.

`kubectl cp` of a 3 GiB file from a pod on a stock kind v1.37.0 cluster, the connection between the apiserver and the kubelet killed 5 s in (`ss -K` on the node), one run per cell:

| | kubectl from master | kubectl with the client-go change |
|---|---|---|
| SPDY, `--retries=3` | `Resuming copy at 728108032 bytes, retry 1/3`, complete, exit 0 | `error: connection closed before the command's status was received; the output may be incomplete`, exit 1, no resume |
| WebSocket, `--retries=3` | `error: error reading from error stream: next reader: websocket: close 1006 (abnormal closure): unexpected EOF`, exit 1, no resume | same |

#### What did you expect to happen?

`--retries` resumes after a cut connection on either transport; that is what it was added for in #104792 (#60140).

#### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. A kind cluster and a pod with a large file (`head -c 3221225472 /dev/zero > /tmp/big`).
2. `kubectl cp --retries=3 pod:/tmp/big ./big`
3. A few seconds in, on the node: `ss -K sport = :10250`, which kills the apiserver's connection to the kubelet.

#### Anything else we need to know?

The fix is in `TarPipe.initReadFrom`: when `MaxTries != 0`, close the pipe with the exec's error instead of calling `CheckErr`, so that `Read` retries; an exit status from `tar` (`utilexec.ExitError`) stays fatal. That raises the question of which errors are worth a retry, and whether `--retries=-1` needs a backoff or a stop when no byte was copied since the last attempt, since a persistent error (the pod is gone) would otherwise retry in a tight loop. I can send the PR once the client-go change has landed.

#### Kubernetes version

kubectl built from master (e234a6f) against kind v1.37.0 (containerd 2.3.4).

title: kubectl create ingress panics when a rule path contains a comma
body:
### What happened?

`kubectl create ingress` panics when a `--rule` path contains a comma.
No cluster is needed; `--dry-run=client` is enough:

```console
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a,b=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1

goroutine 1 [running]:
k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create.buildHTTPIngressPath(...)
	k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go:396 +0x168
k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create.(*CreateIngressOptions).buildIngressRules(...)
	k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go:368 +0xd0
k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create.(*CreateIngressOptions).buildIngressSpec(...)
	k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go:312 +0xcc
```

A comma is a legal URL path character (a sub-delim in RFC 3986), and
`ruleRegex` accepts it: the path group is `(?P<path>/.*)`. So the rule
passes `Validate`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/400031d6953/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go#L223

The builders then discard that match and re-split the raw rule string,
treating the first comma as the start of the TLS clause.
`buildIngressRules` cuts the rule at `strings.Split(rule, ",")[0]`,
leaving `foo.com/a`, so `buildHTTPIngressPath` finds no `=` and indexes
past the end of the slice:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/400031d6953/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go#L365
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/400031d6953/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go#L396

`buildTLSRules` does the same split and reads the remainder as a TLS
clause:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/400031d6953/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_ingress.go#L324

So validation and construction parse the same rule differently.

The panic is the loud case. A path that also carries `=` and `:` is
accepted and silently builds a different object than the one asked for:

```console
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a=b:c,d=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: ing
spec:
  rules:
  - host: foo.com
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: b
            port:
              name: c
        path: /a
        pathType: Exact
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - foo.com
    secretName: svc:8080
status:
  loadBalancer: {}
```

The backend is `b:c` on path `/a` instead of `svc:8080` on
`/a=b:c,d`, and there is a TLS block with `secretName: svc:8080` that
was never requested. No error, no warning.

### What did you expect to happen?

The rule parsed the way `ruleRegex` reads it: the TLS clause is the
optional trailing `,tls[=secret]`, not the first comma anywhere in the
rule. For `foo.com/a,b=svc:8080`:

```yaml
spec:
  rules:
  - host: foo.com
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: svc
            port:
              number: 8080
        path: /a,b
        pathType: Exact
```

and no `tls` block, since `,tls` is absent.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

No cluster required. Each of these panics:

```console
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a,b=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="/path,x=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a,b=svc:8080,tls=s1" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
```

For the silent misparse:

```console
$ kubectl create ingress ing --rule="foo.com/a=b:c,d=svc:8080" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml
```

At the unit level, adding a `TestCreateIngress` case with the rule
`foo.com/a,b=svc:8080` panics against master.

### Anything else we need to know?

Long-standing: the double parse dates from the original
`create ingress` implementation, and the code is unchanged on master
at 400031d6953.

A PR follows that matches each rule once with the compiled `ruleRegex`
and builds the spec from its named groups, so the parse that validates
a rule is the parse that builds it. It carries regression tests for
both the panic and the misparse.

Found through AI-assisted code review. The transcripts above are real
output from kubectl v1.36.0 and from a `./cmd/kubectl` build of master
at 400031d6953.

/kind bug
/sig cli

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version --client
Client Version: v1.36.0
Kustomize Version: v5.8.1
```

Also reproduced with a source build of master at 400031d6953:

```console
$ ./kubectl version --client
Client Version: v0.0.0-master+$Format:%H$
Kustomize Version: v5.8.1
```

</details>

<details>

title: cloud-provider HasClusterID related functionality should have better documentation in the code
Introduce model-based correctness and linearizability testing for k8s storage
body:
### What would you like to be added?

We would like to introduce model-based correctness testing suite for Kubernetes storage (`k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage`), modeled after the [robustness testing approach used in etcd](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/tree/main/tests/robustness#etcd-robustness-testing).

This initiative introduces exploratory property-based and linearizability testing alongside existing table-driven tests to continuously verify consistency and watch invariants across concurrent reads, writes, watches, and cache invalidations.

### Steps


#### Step 1: Minimal Linearizability Model & Baseline Correctness Suite
- Build a formal sequential specification (`KVModel`) for Kubernetes key-value semantics with `ResourceVersion` tracking using [Porcupine](https://github.com/anishathalye/porcupine).
- Implement a concurrent exploratory traffic harness to execute randomized operations against storage implementations and verify strict blackbox linearizability.
- Validate baseline `etcd3` and `cacher` implementations under concurrent workloads.

Progress:

* [ ] Create - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141729, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141996
    * [x] New key
    * [x] Existing key returns KeyExists
    * [x] Object with ResourceVersion set
    * [ ] TTL
* [x] Get - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141729, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141996, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142591
    * [x] Existing key
    * [x] Missing key returns NotFound
    * [x] IgnoreNotFound
    * [x] ResourceVersion
        * [x] ""
        * [x] "0"
        * [x] N
* [ ] Delete - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141729, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141996, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142734
    * [x] Existing key
    * [x] Missing key returns NotFound
    * [x] Precondition on UID
    * [x] Precondition on ResourceVersion
    * [x] validateDeletion - #142734
    * [x] cachedExistingObject - #142734
    * [ ] Unsafe delete (ExpectTransformOrDecodeError)
* [ ] Updates - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142089
    * [x] Existing key
    * [x] Missing key returns NotFound
    * [x] No-op update
    * [x] Precondition on UID
    * [x] cachedExistingObject
    * [x] Concurrent updates to the same key
    * [x] Precondition on ResourceVersion
    * [x] ignoreNotFound
    * [x] UpdateFunc error
    * [x] ResponseMeta passed to UpdateFunc
    * [ ] TTL returned by UpdateFunc
* [ ] Watch - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142117, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142381, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142407, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142479, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142546, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142682, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142688
    * [ ] ResourceVersion
        * [x] "1" - #142117
        * [x] "", "0", current, past, future - #142407
        * [ ] Too old (410)
    * [x] Scope
        * [x] Cluster-wide
        * [x] Namespace
        * [x] Single object (Recursive=false)
        * [x] Namespace whose name is a prefix of another (unit test only)
    * [ ] Selector
        * [x] Validator - #142479
        * [x] Label selector in traffic - #142688
        * [x] Field selector in traffic, indexed and not - #142688
        * [ ] Shard selector
    * [x] AllowWatchBookmarks
        * [x] Validator - #142381, #142682
        * [x] Traffic
    * [x] SendInitialEvents
        * [x] false
        * [x] true (WatchList) - #142546
    * [ ] Guarantees
        * [x] Reliable delivery - #142381, #142682
        * [ ] Consistent start for ResourceVersion ""
        * [ ] Liveness
* [ ] List - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/142720
    * [ ] ResourceVersion
        * [x] ""
        * [x] "0"
        * [x] N, NotOlderThan
        * [x] N, Exact
        * [ ] Too old (410)
    * [x] Scope
        * [x] Cluster-wide
        * [x] Namespace
        * [x] Single object (Recursive=false)
        * [x] Namespace whose name is a prefix of another (unit test only)
    * [ ] Selector
        * [x] Label - #142720
        * [x] Field - #142720
        * [ ] Shard
    * [ ] Pagination
        * [ ] Limit
        * [ ] Continue
* [ ] Other methods
    * [ ] GetCurrentResourceVersion
    * [ ] Stats
    * [ ] RequestWatchProgress
    * [ ] CompactRevision
* [ ] Failure injection
    * [ ] Compaction / History Eviction
        * [x] Small watchCache history window (`EventsHistoryWindow = 50ms`)
        * [x] Watch starting at evicted RV (`410 Expired` in `cacher`)
        * [x] Stalled / slow live watch overtaken by history eviction (`410 Expired` in `cacher`)
        * [x] Slow watch in initial history replay (`processInterval`) overtaken by history eviction (`errCacheIntervalInvalidated` / `410 Expired` in `cacher`)
        * [ ] Periodic etcd compaction (`etcd3`)
        * [ ] List at compacted RV (`410 Expired`)
    * [ ] Watch cache re-initialization
        * [ ] Reflector relist (`watchCache.Replace` + `terminateAllWatchers`) during active traffic & stalled watches
    * [x] Slow watcher (`WatcherBehavior`)
        * [x] Fast drainer reconnecting (`WatcherFast` / `draining-companion`)
        * [x] Never-draining stalled companion reconnecting (`WatcherStalled` / `stalled-once`, `stalled-reconnecting`)
        * [x] Stall-and-resume hiccup reader (`WatcherHiccup`: live -> `unsynced` -> `syncPass` catch-up -> `resync` -> live, or `410 Expired` if overtaken)
        * [x] Paced slow drainer (`WatcherSlow`: partial cohort progress / `reofferPending` across multiple `syncPass` runs)
    * [ ] etcd restart and timeouts

#### Step 2: Storage Request Classification & Coverage Measurement
- Classify operations across four core verbs (`Get`, `List`, `Watch` .. ) across ~80 distinct API states (covering `ResourceVersion` variations, `ResourceVersionMatch` modes, pagination/continue tokens, selector predicates, preconditions, and terminal error codes).
- Provide a zero-dependency, non-invasive decorator (`coverage.Wrap`) to quantify and report API state coverage scorecards on existing and new storage test suites.

#### Step 3: Progressive Model Expansion & Invariant Verification
- Expand the model and test harness to cover:
  - Multi-level key hierarchies and prefix listings.
  - Watch stream invariants: event ordering, bookmark continuity, label/field selector transitions (`Added`, `Modified`, `Deleted`), and slow watcher ring buffer overflow (410 Gone handling).
  - Disruptive lifecycle events: watch cache reinitialization (`watchCache.Replace()` / `terminateAllWatchers`), compaction, and reflector resets.

---

### Code Layout & Dependencies

```
staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/testing
    ├── coverage/                 # Standalone classification and scorecard library (zero external deps)
    └── correctness/              # Formal models and traffic generation
testing/integration/apiserver/correctness - Location of the test
```

As testing linearizability requires dependency on `github.com/anishathalye/porcupine` we will try to put the test under testing package to avoid introducing additional dependency on all users of apiserver library


### Why is this needed?

1. **Blind Spots in Table-Driven Tests**: Existing storage unit and integration tests primarily target specific known code paths. They do not effectively explore race conditions, lock contention, or interleaved state changes across concurrent readers, writers, and watchers.
2. **Confidence in Advanced Storage Features**: With ongoing optimizations (e.g., `WatchList`, `ListFromCacheSnapshot`, `EtcdRangeStream`), subtle correctness bugs (such as stale list returns, broken bookmark continuity, or silent event drops during reflector relists) can easily go undetected without model-driven verification.
3. **Quantifiable Test Coverage**: Storage APIs have a high-dimensional configuration space (`ResourceVersionMatch`, `Continue`, `Limit`, `Predicate`, `Preconditions`). Classifying requests directly from `storage.Interface` allows measuring coverage of existing test suites and ensures no critical API state combinations are left untested.

/cc @liggitt @rpb-ant @nami-ant @mborsz

title: Slow garbage collector informer sync can cause incorrectly deleted orphans
body:
### What happened?

After deleting a statefulset with --cascade=orphan, the garbage collector added the orphan finalizer, and then removed it from the statefulset, without removing the sts as the ownerReference from its pods. About a minute later, the garbage collector deleted those pods because their owner no longer existed.

This happened during a kube-controller-manager leadership change. What happened was that the pod monitor/informer was much slower to sync than the statefulset monitor, so garbage collection proceeded without a fully accurate dependency graph, where it likely saw a statefulset with no dependents. We have ~120k chunky pods in our cluster, and so pod syncing was regularly taking ~35 seconds, which is greater than the timeout of 30s.

This is a result of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125796, which added the 30s timeout.

### What did you expect to happen?

The statefulset should not have been deleted before its pods had their ownerRef's removed

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I reproduced this in kind. The bug needs the pods LIST to take >30s. I was not able to do this with pods alone, as 300k pods synced in 9.5s, but in theory it is possible with a large amount of pods, but I couldn't get to that before using too much memory. Instead, I briefly removed the controller manager's list pod permissions
1. Create a kind cluster
2. Create a statefulset
3. Stop the controller manager
4. Delete the statefulset with `--cascade=orphan`
5. Remove the controller manager's list on pods:
```
kubectl get clusterrole system:kube-controller-manager -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.resourceVersion)' > kcm-role.orig.json
kubectl api-resources --verbs=list,watch -o name | grep -vx pods |
  jq -R -s --slurpfile role kcm-role.orig.json '
    [split("\n")[] | select(length > 0) | split(".") | {r: .[0], g: (.[1:] | join("."))}]
    | group_by(.g)
    | map({apiGroups: [.[0].g], resources: map(.r), verbs: ["list", "watch"]}) as $new
    | $role[0]
    | .rules = ([.rules[] | select(.apiGroups != ["*"] or .resources != ["*"])] + $new)' |
  kubectl replace -f -
kubectl auth can-i list pods -A --as=$ROLE    # no
``` 
6. Start the controller manager and wait 30s
7. Restore controller manager perms:
```
kubectl replace -f kcm-role.orig.json
kubectl -n repro get pods -w -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,DELETED:.metadata.deletionTimestamp,OWNER:.metadata.ownerReferences[0].uid
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: [Flaking Test] E2eNode Suite [It] [sig-node] [DRA] [Feature:DynamicResourceAllocation] Two resource Kubelet Plugins must call NodeUnprepareResources again if it's in progress for one plugin when Kubelet restarts [Serial]
Allow scaling up to meet PDB constraints
body:
**What would you like to be added**:

Currently if you have a PDB spec like `minAvailable: 1`, and a HPA defining minReplicas=1 and maxReplicas=N, you may end up in a scenario where disruptions get "stuck" if the HPA has scaled to 1. At any point an increase in load could cause the HPA to scale up to 2+, allowing the PDB to be satisfied, which leads to a weird scenario where a disruption can only occur if there is high load.

Ideally, the PDB would be able to trigger the HPA to scale up to meet constraints. For example, if I have 1 replica and a disruption is triggered, scale up a new replica first, then terminate the old one. Given an HPA is in place, I have already clearly specified I am OK with my pod being scaled up, so this shouldn't have negative impact on stateful workloads.

Some more context: https://github.com/istio/istio/issues/12602

title: PreFilter Skip can be invalidated by a reprieved victim
body:
### What happened?

Currently, unlike single-pod preemption (which reuses the CycleState from the initial scheduling cycle when all victims were still in the snapshot), `selectVictimsOnDomain` first removes all candidateVictims from mutableLister and then calls podGroupSchedulingFunc(ctx), which runs a fresh PreFilter on the victim-free snapshot.

Now looking into InterPodAffinity PreFilter plugin:
```
incomingPodHasNoTerms := len(s.podInfo.GetRequiredAffinityTerms()) == 0 && len(s.podInfo.GetRequiredAntiAffinityTerms()) == 0
if len(s.existingClusterWideAntiAffinityCounts) == 0 && incomingPodHasNoTerms && !mustEvaluateHostScopedAntiAffinity {
    return nil, fwk.NewStatus(fwk.Skip)
}
cycleState.Write(preFilterStateKey, s)
```

- Suppose preemptor pod P has no affinity/anti-affinity terms (incomingPodHasNoTerms == true), no non-victim pod in the cluster has required anti-affinity, but a candidate victim V has required anti-affinity matching P.
- Because V was already removed from the snapshot before podGroupSchedulingFunc(ctx) ran, InterPodAffinity.PreFilter sees len(s.existingClusterWideAntiAffinityCounts) == 0 and !mustEvaluateHostScopedAntiAffinity, so it returns fwk.Skip (and never writes preFilterStateKey to cycleState)!
Consequently, "InterPodAffinity" is added to assignment.GetCycleState().GetSkipFilterPlugins().

Then, during reprieveVictim` both RunPreFilterExtensionAddPod and RunFilterPlugins check:
```
if state.GetSkipFilterPlugins().Has(pl.Name()) {
    continue
}
```
So when victim V (with anti-affinity against P) is reprieved, RunPreFilterExtensionAddPod skips InterPodAffinity.AddPod, and RunFilterPlugins skips InterPodAffinity.Filter! Victim V is erroneously reprieved in violation of its required anti-affinity!


This is the problem only for Pod Anti-Affinity, as this is the only bi-directional constraint.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pod Anti-Affinity to be honored. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Try scheduling a pod (without any constraints) that is matched against anti-affinity rules from all currently running pods (lower-priority).

### Anything else we need to know?

title: [Scheduler] DefaultPreemption PreEnqueue can limit the number of events that moves preemptor
body:
### What happened?

Follow up from: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141694

When the defaultPreemption blocks a transition for pod from backoff/unschedulable queue to active queue via PreEnqueue, it becomes a gating plugin. The GatingPluginEvents become only [AssignedPod/Delete]. This can be only a subset of events that could originally move pod to active queue based on the list of unschedulable queue.

The code that cares only about gating plugin events: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3338aac0c6f3828e26008458c5cd93ec4fdc97c0/pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L1822-L1826

Events for unschedulable plugins are evaluated in isEntityWorthRequeuing.


### What did you expect to happen?

I expected that after preemption PreEnqueue blocks the transition, the events that pod reacts to is still the same set of events from unschedulable plugins

title: Migrate DRA components to support granular authorization on status updates
body:
/triage accepted
/sig auth node network
/wg device-management
/good-first-issue

@liggitt @aojea @dims @pohly @johnbelamaric 

AI generated migration guide with list of potentially impacted components.

---

# DRA Granular Status Authorization: Migration Guide

Starting in Kubernetes v1.36, the `DRAResourceClaimGranularStatusAuthorization` feature gate
(beta, on-by-default) enforces fine-grained authorization checks for `ResourceClaim` status
updates. Components that previously only needed `update`/`patch` on `resourceclaims/status`
now require additional permissions on **synthetic subresources** depending on which status
fields they modify.

Reference: #134947, https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/55070

---

## What changed

| Old permission | New additional permission required | Who needs it |
|---|---|---|
| `resourceclaims/status` `update`/`patch` | `resourceclaims/binding` `update`/`patch` | Schedulers, allocation controllers (anything modifying `status.allocation` or `status.reservedFor`) |
| `resourceclaims/status` `update`/`patch` | `resourceclaims/driver` `associated-node:update`/`associated-node:patch` | Node-local DRA drivers (ServiceAccount bound to a specific node via pod-bound token) |
| `resourceclaims/status` `update`/`patch` | `resourceclaims/driver` `arbitrary-node:update`/`arbitrary-node:patch` | Control-plane DRA drivers, network controllers, or any component managing device status across nodes |

The existing `resourceclaims/status` permission is **still required** — it remains the "front door".
The new synthetic subresources are **additional** checks on top of it.

These new permissions can be added **now** in preparation for 1.36, they are inert in earlier versions of Kubernetes.

---

## Migration by component type

### Node-local DRA drivers

These run as DaemonSets with a ServiceAccount whose token is bound to the node (via a pod
scheduled on that node). They update `status.devices` for their own driver.

**Add this rule to the driver's ClusterRole:**

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["resource.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["resourceclaims/driver"]
  verbs: ["associated-node:update", "associated-node:patch"]
  resourceNames: ["<your-driver-name>"]  # e.g. "dra.example.com"
```

**Keep the existing rule:**

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["resource.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["resourceclaims/status"]
  verbs: ["get", "update", "patch"]
```

### Control-plane DRA drivers / multi-node controllers

These run as Deployments (not node-bound). They update `status.devices` for their driver
from a central controller.

**Add this rule to the controller's ClusterRole:**

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["resource.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["resourceclaims/driver"]
  verbs: ["arbitrary-node:update", "arbitrary-node:patch"]
  resourceNames: ["<your-driver-name>"]  # e.g. "dra.example.com"
```

**Keep the existing rule:**

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["resource.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["resourceclaims/status"]
  verbs: ["get", "update", "patch"]
```

### Schedulers

These modify `status.allocation` and `status.reservedFor` when binding claims to nodes.

**Add this rule to the scheduler's ClusterRole:**

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["resource.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["resourceclaims/binding"]
  verbs: ["update", "patch"]
```

**Keep the existing rule:**

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["resource.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["resourceclaims/status"]
  verbs: ["get", "update", "patch"]
```

> Note: The built-in `system:kube-scheduler` ClusterRole is updated automatically
> by the bootstrap policy when the feature gate is enabled. Only custom schedulers
> need manual updates.

### Operators / virtual clusters that proxy all ResourceClaim operations

These need **all** of the above depending on what operations they proxy.

**Add both rules:**

```yaml
- apiGroups: ["resource.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["resourceclaims/binding"]
  verbs: ["update", "patch"]
- apiGroups: ["resource.k8s.io"]
  resources: ["resourceclaims/driver"]
  verbs: ["associated-node:update", "associated-node:patch", "arbitrary-node:update", "arbitrary-node:patch"]
```

### Components that only read status or manage non-status fields

No changes needed. The new checks only apply to **writes** to `status.allocation`,
`status.reservedFor`, and `status.devices`.

---

### DRA Drivers

title: kube-apiserver built with Go 1.27 returns 431 for impersonated or front-proxy users with about 500 groups
body:
### What happened?

We're reporting this ahead of v1.38 because it only appears when several conditions combine, and it's easy to miss until someone with a large group membership hits it.

Go 1.27 added `http.Server.MaxHeaderValueCount` with a default of 500 ([golang/go#79936](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/79936)). Repeated header lines are counted individually. kube-apiserver does not set this field, and the identity headers it accepts carry one group per header line:

- `Impersonate-Group` (user impersonation)
- `X-Remote-Group` (request-header authentication, used by authenticating proxies)

As a result, kube-apiserver v1.38.0-alpha.1 (go1.27.1) returns `431 Request Header Fields Too Large` for requests that impersonate, or are proxied on behalf of, a user with about 500 groups. For the curl request below, 495 groups produce 431 over HTTP/2 but 200 over HTTP/1.1, and 500 groups produce 431 over both; the exact threshold depends on the other request headers. v1.37.1 (go1.26.8) accepts the same requests, tested up to 1,000 groups.

The rejection happens in `net/http` before Kubernetes request handlers run. In our run with Metadata-level auditing and default log verbosity, the rejected requests had no audit record and no related kube-apiserver log message.

Go 1.27 has no `GODEBUG` override for this limit; one was proposed and declined ([golang/go#80020](https://github.com/golang/go/issues/80020)). Accepting the same repeated headers on a Go 1.27 server requires setting `MaxHeaderValueCount`.

Who is affected, as far as we can tell: only requests whose groups are carried in headers (impersonation, request-header authentication, and requests kube-apiserver proxies to aggregated API servers), for users with roughly 500 or more groups, on servers built with Go 1.27. Users with fewer groups are unaffected. Groups taken from client certificates, OIDC or webhook token authentication are not sent to kube-apiserver as headers, although aggregated API servers still receive them that way. We hit this with an enterprise directory in which some users belong to more than 1,000 groups.

### What did you expect to happen?

Requests for users with several hundred to over a thousand groups keep working through impersonation and request-header authentication, as they do with Go 1.26 builds, or the limit becomes explicit and documented rather than an implicit `net/http` default.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Start etcd (listening on `127.0.0.1:2379`) and kube-apiserver v1.38.0-alpha.1 with a static token in `system:masters`, then wait until `/readyz` returns 200:

   ```sh
   openssl genrsa -out sa.key 2048 && openssl rsa -in sa.key -pubout -out sa.pub
   echo 'admintoken,admin,admin-uid,"system:masters"' > tokens.csv
   kube-apiserver --etcd-servers=http://127.0.0.1:2379 --bind-address=127.0.0.1 --secure-port=6443 \
     --cert-dir=./serving --token-auth-file=tokens.csv --authorization-mode=RBAC \
     --service-account-issuer=https://kubernetes.default.svc --service-account-key-file=sa.pub \
     --service-account-signing-key-file=sa.key --service-cluster-ip-range=10.96.0.0/16
   ```

2. Impersonate a user with 495 groups:

   ```sh
   {
     echo 'header = "Authorization: Bearer admintoken"'
     echo 'header = "Impersonate-User: alice"'
     echo 'header = "Impersonate-Group: system:masters"'
     for g in $(seq 2 495); do echo "header = \"Impersonate-Group: group-$g\""; done
   } > impersonate.cfg
   curl -sk --http2 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_version} %{http_code}\n' -K impersonate.cfg \
     https://127.0.0.1:6443/api/v1/namespaces/default
   ```

   This prints `2 431` (curl must support HTTP/2; check `curl -V`). With 490 groups, or with kube-apiserver v1.37.1, it prints `2 200`.

We also tested request-header authentication separately: `--requestheader-client-ca-file`, `--requestheader-allowed-names`, `--requestheader-username-headers=X-Remote-User` and `--requestheader-group-headers=X-Remote-Group`, with `X-Remote-User` and repeated `X-Remote-Group` headers sent using a client certificate signed by that CA. It gave the same results as impersonation.

Results (`GET /api/v1/namespaces/default`, the group count includes `system:masters`):

| Groups | v1.37.1 (go1.26.8), HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 | v1.38.0-alpha.1 (go1.27.1), HTTP/2 | v1.38.0-alpha.1 (go1.27.1), HTTP/1.1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 480 | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| 490 | 200 | 200 | 200 |
| 495 | 200 | 431 | 200 |
| 500 | 200 | 431 | 431 |
| 1000 | 200 | 431 | 431 |

Impersonation and request-header authentication gave identical results in every case. Other request headers count toward the same limit, which is why the threshold is slightly below 500 groups.

### Anything else we need to know?

- `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/secure_serving.go` sets `MaxHeaderBytes` (1 MiB) but not `MaxHeaderValueCount`. Under Go 1.27, `golang.org/x/net/http2.ConfigureServer` (v0.59.0) hands HTTP/2 to the `net/http` server, so the limit applies to both protocols.
- kube-aggregator forwards the user's groups to aggregated API servers as separate `X-Remote-Group` headers ([round_trippers.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/039223d3e2a1c6f5b1422c95fb396ff8c31d2619/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/round_trippers.go#L125-L142)). An aggregated API server built with Go 1.27 that keeps the default limit may therefore reject such requests. We measured this internally with a KubeVirt virt-api build using Go 1.27; the reproduction above exercises kube-apiserver only.
- Release branches 1.34 to 1.37 currently build with Go 1.26. A future Go 1.27 update on those branches would bring this behaviour with it.
- Authenticating proxies can forward hundreds of directory groups for a user; requests in that range are affected as shown above.
- Clients cannot reduce the header count by comma-joining groups: that format is not supported for `X-Remote-Group` or `Impersonate-Group` (#82468, #94683). #82468 also discusses a single structured user-info header, which would avoid the per-group header count entirely.
- A possible direction: an explicit, bounded and, if appropriate, configurable `MaxHeaderValueCount` in `k8s.io/apiserver` secure serving that supports the intended group sizes while keeping protection against floods of small headers, tested over both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. We're happy to help with a fix once there's agreement on the approach.

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery
/sig auth
